page: Google Cloud Platform ct6e-standard-8t is a specialized accelerator instance designed for machine learning workloads. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 360 dedicated virtual CPUs and 1440.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The defining characteristic of the ct6e-standard-8t is the integration of eight Google TPU v6e accelerators, delivering a combined 256 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. This hardware configuration is specifically engineered for accelerating deep learning training and inference tasks. An architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, meaning all data persistence and dataset staging must rely on network-attached storage or cloud storage buckets.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ct6e-standard-8t offers a dense consolidation of compute resources and specialized TPU accelerators on a single instance, reducing the overhead associated with managing multi-node clusters for medium-to-large machine learning tasks. This server is optimized for workloads such as large language model training, transformer-based neural network inference, data science pipelines, and large-scale parallel matrix computations.
description: Google Cloud Platform ct6e-standard-8t is a specialized accelerator instance built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 360 dedicated vCPUs and 1440.0 GB of system memory. Designed for high-throughput machine learning workloads, the server integrates eight Google TPU v6e accelerators with a total of 256 GB of VRAM. It provides a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU but lacks local storage, requiring external network storage solutions for data persistence. This high-density hardware profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for consolidating large-scale deep learning training and inference pipelines. The ct6e-standard-8t is best suited for data science jobs, machine learning model training, and large-scale AI inference workloads.
